data.name: Luban
data.short_meaning: Mythological figure who provided Prophet Ibrahim with the zulafiqar sword
data.long_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Luban is a mythological figure who, upon being asked by Prophet Ibrahim for a weapon to face the enemy, presented him with the Zulfiqar sword, which later became a significant symbol in Shia Islam. The name Luban is derived from the Arabic word ‘al-luban’ meaning ‘resin’ or ‘gum’, symbolizing the resilience and strength of this figure.

data.cultural_impact: Luban is mentioned in various Islamic sources, most notably in the Hadiths, as a noble figure, emphasizing the idea of self-sacrifice and courage. In Shia Islam, Luban is considered part of the prophetic family tree as the son of both Prophet Qais and Prophet Shuayb's sister. Narratives about Luban have been a rich source of inspiration for Islamic art and literature, with many stories, poems, and calligraphic works depicting both his personal struggle and religious devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: Symbolically, Luban’s gift of the Zulfiqar sword to Prophet Ibrahim represents the power of righteous intention, wisdom, and belief in the face of adversity. It underscores the spiritual strength and resilience that lies within each individual when they stay true to their faith and inner convictions. The significance of this story is a reminder of the importance of courage and resolve in the ever-changing landscape of human existence. This ancient tale continues to captivate and inspire Muslims' spiritually, offering a lens to view Islamic values in an insightful and meaningful way.
